A short list of the resources most useful for this course. Please let us know
if there are other links that you think should be included on this page!

Course readings (journal articles and book chapters) are posted on WebCampus.

# Software

- [dagitty](https://www.dagitty.net): free, web-based tool for drawing and
  analyzing causal diagrams (DAGs). No account needed.
- [R](https://www.r-project.org) and [RStudio](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/):
  free software for statistical computing. Optional, for exercise extensions.

# Free books and online texts

- [The Effect](https://theeffectbook.net) (Huntington-Klein): a readable
  introduction to research design and causality.
- [Causal Inference: The Mixtape](https://mixtape.scunning.com) (Cunningham).
- [A Primer to Causal Reasoning About a Complex World](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-59135-8)
  (Johansson et al. 2024; open access).
- [Causation and Manipulability](https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/causation-mani/)
  (Woodward), in the *Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy*.
- [Statistical Rethinking](https://xcelab.net/rm/) (McElreath): book page, with
  links to the free video lectures.

# Reading lists and other courses

- [Causal inference in ecology: readings](https://lauradee.github.io/EcologyCausalInference/readings.html)
  (Laura Dee).

# Help at UNR

- [Weekly "Stats Chats"](https://guides.library.unr.edu/StatsChats) at the UNR
  library: drop-in help with statistics and R.
